summary: Training volume over the last 4 weeks has been very low and inconsistent, with only 9 sessions logged totalling roughly 10 hours across all disciplines — well below what is needed for sub-4h marathon and Ironman preparation. Sleep is severely compromised, with multiple nights under 5 hours and several under 4 hours, and body battery readings frequently in the 20s–40s suggesting chronic under-recovery. The one standout concern is the July 18 run at 179 avg HR (likely near-maximal effort) at 5:02/km, which points to either a hard effort executed without adequate recovery or poor aerobic base fitness at this pace.
suggestions: Prioritise sleep above all else — with marathon 192 days away, chronic sleep deprivation is the single biggest limiter; target a minimum 7 hours per night before adding any training load.

Running pace must be controlled: your easy and long runs should stay at 6:15–6:45/km with HR under 155 bpm; the July 18 effort at 179 bpm avg is a warning sign and should not be repeated in aerobic sessions.

Begin pool swimming sessions immediately — open water swims of 0.1–2km are a start but you have zero pool sessions logged in 4 weeks, and the Ironman swim target of 1:50/100m requires structured technique and pacing work in a controlled environment.

The long Saturday ride planned for Aug 1 (84km, 240 min) represents a significant jump from your last ride (77km on July 20 after a long training gap) — execute it conservatively at Z2 lower end (128–150W) and treat it as an adaptation session, not a fitness test.

Add a short aerobic run (30 min easy at 6:30–6:50/km) in the next 2–3 days to re-establish running frequency before the Wk6 long run on Aug 2; with only 3 runs in 4 weeks, jumping straight to 18.4km carries injury risk.

proposed_changes.proposed_session: Skip the evening cycling session entirely; body battery hit 2 today (Jul 30) indicating severe fatigue — treat today as full rest after strength work only if energy allows.
proposed_changes.reason: Body battery of 2 on July 30 signals the athlete is running on empty and adding a 90-min evening session risks compounding fatigue going into the weekend's critical long sessions.

proposed_changes.proposed_session: Reduce to 60–65km @ 128–155W (Z2 lower end only), approximately 180–200 min; no Z3 Tempo blocks this week.
proposed_changes.reason: With only one ride in the last 4 weeks and severely depleted recovery scores, a full 84km effort is premature and risks injury or illness before the training block properly begins.

proposed_changes.proposed_session: Reduce to 12–14km @ 6:30–6:45/km, keeping HR strictly under 155 bpm; extend only if feeling genuinely strong after the first 10km.
proposed_changes.reason: With only 3 runs totalling ~16km in the last 4 weeks, jumping to 18.4km as the first weekend long run significantly elevates injury risk.

proposed_changes.proposed_session: Replace with a steady Z2 endurance ride, 128–155W, 45–50 min — no threshold intervals this week.
proposed_changes.reason: Threshold cycling intervals require a solid aerobic base and fresh legs; introducing Z4 intensity this early after a multi-week low-volume period risks overreach and poor adaptation.

proposed_changes.proposed_session: Reduce to 3x5min @ 210–244W (Z4 Threshold) with 4min Z1 recovery, total ~50 min, only if Wk6–7 have been completed as planned and recovery scores are above 50.
proposed_changes.reason: Progressive introduction of threshold work (3 reps before 5 reps) reduces injury and overtraining risk given the athlete's recent very low training load.

proposed_changes.proposed_session: Cap at 16km @ 6:15–6:45/km only if the Wk6 long run went well; otherwise repeat 12–14km again before progressing distance.
proposed_changes.reason: Building long run distance by 4km per week from a low base is aggressive; a more conservative 2km weekly increment (from a reduced Wk6 baseline) will reduce overuse injury risk while still progressing toward marathon fitness.
